PlayerGameLaunchController

class PlayerGameLaunchController(view, message_service=None, service=None, calibration_service=None)[source]

Bases: QObject

Controller of the game launch window.

Validates the selection and the calibration, starts the chosen game as a separate process and stops it when the window closes.

Parameters:
viewPlayerGameLaunchView

The game launch dialog.

message_serviceMessageService | None, optional

Service used to show messages. Default is None, which creates MessageService(view).

servicePlayerGameLaunchService | None, optional

Launch service. Default is None, which creates a new one.

calibration_serviceCalibrationService | None, optional

Calibration service. Default is None, which creates a new one.

Attributes:
viewPlayerGameLaunchView

The game launch dialog.

msgMessageService

Service used to show messages.

servicePlayerGameLaunchService

Launch service.

calibration_serviceCalibrationService

Calibration service.

current_processsubprocess.Popen | None

Process of the running game, if any.

monitor_timerQTimer | None

Timer that checks whether the game has started.

Notes

All messages are translated with self.tr().

handle_cancel()[source]

Close the window, asking first if a game is running.

Notes

“No” is the default answer. The game itself is stopped by cleanup when the window closes.

handle_game_info()[source]

Show the developers, version and years of the selected game.

A warning is shown when the metadata has no developers or version.

launch_game()[source]

Validate the selection and start the selected game.

Notes

A player, a professional and a game must be selected, no game may be running, the game entry point must exist and both the calibration points and the hardware calibration must be saved; then _verify_hardware_configuration is checked.

The game runs in its folder with the arguments --lang, --player_id and --professional_id; .py and .pyw entry points run with the current Python interpreter. On Windows it starts in a new process group. The buttons stay disabled until the game is up (checked every 500 ms) or for at most 7 s.

is_game_running()[source]

Check whether the game process is still running.

Returns:
bool

True if a game process exists and has not exited.

update_tooltip(index)[source]

Show the tooltip of the selected game on the game combo box.

Parameters:
indexint

Index of the selected game; negative values are ignored.

cleanup()[source]

Stop the game and all its child processes.

Notes

Called when the window closes. With psutil, the children and the game are terminated, and those still alive after 2 s are killed; without it, only the game process is terminated (and killed on error). The monitor timer is stopped and the buttons are restored in every case.
